metadata.title: Collect 13% On CIEN Stock Now, Own It 60% Cheaper If It Dips

content.text:
Here is a way to collect an immediate income stream from the networking boom, which you keep no matter what, while lining up a chance to buy a key supplier at a deep discount if it ever gets there.
After a blistering run, shares of optical networking specialist Ciena (CIEN) have pulled back from their highs, despite the company recently posting a monster quarter. For investors who see opportunity in the AI-driven demand for data plumbing but are wary of chasing a hot stock, this creates an interesting setup for a trade that pays you to be patient.
13.5% annualized yield at a 60% margin of safety, by selling put options.
-
Sell a put option on CIEN expiring 6/17/2027, with a strike price of $175.
-
Collect roughly $1,245 in premium per contract (each contract covers 100 shares).
-
That works out to about 8.5% annualized on the $17,500 of cash you set aside to secure the trade.
-
Park that cash in a money market or savings account earning roughly 5.0%, and your total yield climbs to about 13.5%.
-
And if CIEN falls below $175, you buy it at $175, already a 60% discount to today's $432.05, and after the premium, your entry drops to about $162.55 a share, about a 62% discount to today's price.
Two Outcomes, You Keep The Premium Either Way
If CIEN stays above $175 through 6/17/2027, the put expires worthless, and you simply keep the full $1,245 premium. That is about 7.1% on the $17,500 you set aside over 308 days, roughly 8.5% annualized, while that same collateral keeps earning about 5.0% money-market yield on top, for the 13.5% total above. You never buy the stock and keep the income, free to do it again.
If CIEN closes below $175, you are assigned and buy 100 shares at $175. The $1,245 premium you already pocketed lowers your effective cost to about $162.55 a share, roughly a 62% discount to today's price, though if the stock has fallen further by then you would be holding a paper loss.
So what happens if CIEN really does close below $175, and you are the one buying? Then everything rests on a single question.
What You Would Actually Be Buying
So, how comfortable would you be owning this business if it got cheaper? Because that is the real question. If the stock falls below your chosen price, you are on the hook to buy it. The bull case is straightforward and powerful. Ciena is riding a massive wave of network infrastructure spending, with fiscal second-quarter revenue jumping 40% year-on-year to $1.57 billion. Management is guiding for full-year 2026 revenue growth of 32% at the midpoint. The demand appears locked in, with the company's backlog swelling to $7.7 billion, providing what the CFO calls "excellent visibility into 2027." Ciena is also landing key design wins with the world's biggest cloud providers for next-generation systems like its RLS Hyper-Rail platform, positioning it at the heart of the AI buildout.
